actions.text: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Public Lands, Forests, and Mining. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-305.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

subcommittees.name: Public Lands, Forests, and Mining Subcommittee

dimensions.assessment: Affects residents, conservationists, recreationists, and sportsmen in Montana, as well as federal land management agencies.
dimensions.evidence: enhanced sportsmen opportunities in the backcountry of Montana

dimensions.assessment: Removes wilderness study protections from approximately 103,960 total acres, enabling new management options such as wildlife habitat and wildfire mitigation projects.
dimensions.evidence: The approximately 81,000 acres of land comprising the Middle Fork Judith Wilderness Study Area... shall no longer be subject to section 3(a)

dimensions.assessment: Changes the legal framework for managing specific public lands without specifying direct federal appropriations or revenue changes.
dimensions.evidence: shall be managed in accordance with the applicable land and resource management plan most recently adopted

dimensions.assessment: Amends the application of the Montana Wilderness Study Act of 1977 and the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 for designated parcels in Montana.
dimensions.evidence: shall no longer be subject to section 3(a) of the Montana Wilderness Study Act of 1977

dimensions.assessment: Permanently releases the specified wilderness study areas to be managed under standard agency land and resource management plans.
dimensions.evidence: shall no longer be subject to section 3(a) of the Montana Wilderness Study Act of 1977

missing_information: Estimated administrative costs for implementing new land management plans on the released acreage
importance_detail.rationale: The bill releases over 100,000 acres of federal land in Montana from wilderness study area status, altering land management mandates for specific public tracts.
